title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report
abstract: arXiv:2611.13563v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Edge NPU performance depends not only on hardware capabilities, but also on model transformation and the overall deployment pipeline. We propose a benchmarking methodology that separates these effects by comparing three configurations: Baseline, Vendor Guided NPU Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E), where VG-NPU preserves common model I/O and host-side processing while VG-E2E follows the vendor-native deployment pipeline. We apply this methodology to four edge NPUs and three vision workloads. VG-NPU improves both accuracy and Runtime-call latency in 10 of 12 NPU--workload combinations, whereas VG-E2E reduces System-level latency in all combinations but improves accuracy in only four. Moreover, NPU-level performance rankings do not always match End-to-End rankings, and VG-E2E provides an additional 10.4--70.7\% reduction in System-level latency over VG-NPU. These results demonstrate the importance of evaluating vendor-gui

translated_title: 边缘NPU上厂商引导优化的基准测试：从仅NPU到端到端性能（扩展技术报告）
translated_abstract: 边缘 NPU 的性能不仅取决于硬件能力，还取决于模型转换和整体部署流程。我们提出了一种基准测试方法，通过比较三种配置来分离这些影响：基线配置、厂商引导仅NPU（VG-NPU）和厂商引导端到端（VG-E2E），其中 VG-NPU 保留常见的模型输入/输出和主机端处理，而 VG-E2E 则遵循厂商原生的部署流程。我们将该方法应用于四个边缘 NPU 和三个视觉工作负载。VG-NPU 在 12 个 NPU-工作负载组合中的 10 个中同时改善了准确率和运行时调用延迟，而 VG-E2E 在所有组合中都降低了系统级延迟，但仅在四个组合中改善了准确率。此外，NPU 级别的性能排名并不总是与端到端排名一致，且 VG-E2E 相比 VG-NPU 在系统级延迟上额外提供了 10.4–70.7% 的降低。这些结果表明评估厂商引导优化的端到端效果的重要性。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种通过比较基线、厂商引导仅NPU（VG-NPU）和厂商引导端到端（VG-E2E）三种配置来分离硬件、模型转换与部署流程影响的基准测试方法，发现NPU级性能排名与端到端性能排名可能不一致，且厂商原生部署流程可额外降低10.4–70.7%的系统级延迟。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a benchmarking methodology that separates hardware, model transformation, and deployment pipeline effects by comparing Baseline, VG-NPU, and VG-E2E configurations, revealing that NPU-level performance rankings do not always match end-to-end rankings and that vendor-native deployment pipelines provide an additional 10.4–70.7% reduction in system-level latency.
